name: LightCraft
summary: Develop photos and camera raws from Nextcloud with LightCraft
description:
Open a photo or a camera raw in Files with **Edit in LightCraft** and develop it right in the browser, the way you know from a photo library app: light and colour, curves, colour mixing, detail and noise reduction, lens corrections, crop and straighten, masks and presets.

- The photo is added to your LightCraft library in this browser (once: opening it again shows the same photo, edits and all) and opens with the Edit panel.
- **Export** stores the developed photo (JPEG, PNG, TIFF…) in your Nextcloud: in the photo's folder unless you type another one, and it asks before replacing a file. The original is never changed.
- Optionally, clicking a photo in Files opens it in LightCraft.
readme_features:
- **Edit in LightCraft** appears in the Files action menu of every photo LightCraft reads: JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP, GIF, BMP, JPEG XL and camera raws (DNG, CR2, NEF, ARW).
- The photo is added to your LightCraft library in this browser, then opens with the Edit panel. Opening it again shows the same photo with its edits; your edits stay in the browser's library, as in LightCraft's own web version.
- **Export** stores the developed photo in your Nextcloud. The Export dialog's **Folder** starts as the photo's folder (a path in your Nextcloud such as `/Photos`; type another one to export elsewhere, and missing folders are created), and you're asked before a file there is replaced. The original photo is never changed: an export that would take its name gets ` (edited)` added.
readme_limitations:
- The LightCraft library (your edits, ratings, collections) lives in this browser's storage, not in Nextcloud: back it up with **File › Back Up Library…**, and expect another browser or device to start with an empty library.
- LightCraft runs in one browser tab at a time; close the other tab to open a photo in a new one.
bridge_notes: LightCraft keeps its library in the browser (OPFS or IndexedDB), as its web build always does. `lightcraft:open` carries `path` and a `Blob`; the photo is added to the library like a dropped file (or found there by its content), then selected and shown with the Edit panel. The Export dialog's folder starts as the opened photo's folder on the parent's side, and every export is sent as `lightcraft:save` named by its path there (an export that would replace a photo the parent sent gets ` (edited)` in its name); the parent stores it, creating missing folders, and asks before replacing a file. `lightcraft:dirty` is true while library changes wait to be written to browser storage.
boot_after:
// No separate Chinese font in this build: LightCraft falls back to its other fonts.
	app.start(new Uint8Array())
extra_assets_sh:
# The render worker LightCraft starts by a relative URL.
cp "$SRC/apps/lightcraft-web/worker.js" "$DEST/worker.js"
# LightCraft keeps its asset attributions and the UI font's licence under assets/.
cp "$SRC/assets/ATTRIBUTION.md" "$OUT/LIGHTCRAFT-ATTRIBUTION.md"
cp "$SRC/assets/fonts/OFL-Inter.txt" "$OUT/LIGHTCRAFT-OFL-Inter.txt"
web_extra_rows: | `build.txt`, `build-<hash>/` | The current build: `frame.html` (the page in the editor's iframe, static so LightCraft's relative URLs resolve in its folder), `boot.js`, the glue, the wasm and `worker.js` (render workers) |
